messages.subject: Remove loci, out of Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, from a genclone object
messages.subject_clean: Remove loci, out of Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, from a genclone object
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I created a gencone object by importing a genalex-structured file. I have 2937 SNPs across 42 individuals, comprising 6 populations.  (I treat the SNPs as microsatellite loci in the file, so that 1-4 below represents either A, C, G, or T.):

 2937  42

 Ind   Pop     1       2       3
 4     Crater  3   3   2   2   4   4
 8     Crater  3   3   1   2   4   4

I just ran the hw.test on the loci making up each population - the genclone object is "myData":

myData.hwe.pop <- seppop(myData) %>% lapply(hw.test, B = 0)

I have several loci out of Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, with p values < 0.05, and I would like to remove them. The result of the hw.test is a matrix of these p values over the loci. I am not sure how to remove these same loci, but from the genclone object, since this object has a structure different from a matrix or data frame.  Is it easiest to instead manipulate my original genalex file as a data frame, and then again read this file as a genclone object?

Any help would be appreciated.  Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: Remove loci, out of Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, from a genclone object
messages.subject_clean: Remove loci, out of Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, from a genclone object
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You can subset loci in a genclone or genind object by specifying the "loc" argument using the names or position of the loci. This is documented in the basics tutorial for adegenet (https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/raw/master/tutorials/tutorial-basics.pdf) and the documentation for accessors (http://rpackages.ianhowson.com/cran/adegenet/man/accessors.html).

For example, if your data had the first 100 loci in HWE, you could subset it by doing:

myData[loc = 1:100]

You could even subset with a TRUE/FALSE vector specifying which loci you want to keep.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject: Missing data for genlight object - bug?
messages.subject_clean: Missing data for genlight object - bug?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, (please see note at end of message),

I have nearly sucessfully created a genlight object, except the missing data seems to be a problem.  Missing data (whether set to "", "NA", "0", "-9", or "-") becomes a number and an allele in the genlight object.  Here is my data frame:

> table.test
    X446043 X539052 X614054 X683054 X1520058 X1560020 X1744046 X2197057
188      NA      NA      NA       2       NA       NA        4       NA
189      NA      NA      NA      NA       NA       NA       NA       NA
190       1      NA      NA      NA       NA       NA       NA       NA
191      NA      NA       1      NA       NA        4        4        2
192      NA      NA       1      NA       NA       NA        4       NA
193      NA      NA      NA      NA        3        4       NA       NA
194      NA      NA      NA      NA       NA        4       NA        2
195      NA       2      NA      NA       NA        9       NA        2
171      NA       2       1      NA        3       NA       NA       NA
180       1      NA      NA      NA       NA       NA       NA       NA

Here I am making a genlight object, but it has 0% missing data:

> x <- new("genlight", table.test, parallel = FALSE, NA.char="NA")
> x
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 10 genotypes,  8 binary SNPs, size: 18 Kb
 0 (0 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 10 SNPbin

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  10 individual labels
   @loc.names:  8 locus labels
   @other: a list containing: elements without names

When I print a matrix of this, the NA's have switched to integers here, 3's or 4's:

> as.matrix(x)
    X446043 X539052 X614054 X683054 X1520058 X1560020 X1744046 X2197057
188       3       3       3       1        3        4        1        3
189       3       3       3       3        3        4        3        3
190       1       3       3       3        3        4        3        3
191       3       3       1       3        3        2        1        1
192       3       3       1       3        3        4        1        3
193       3       3       3       3        1        2        3        3
194       3       3       3       3        3        2        3        1
195       3       2       3       3        3        3        3        1
171       3       2       1       3        1        4        3        3
180       1       3       3       3        3        4        3        3

(I tried joining the adgenet forum last week, but I have not yet had any success, so I thought I would try posting my question here.  I have been using genclone objects; however, now that I am using my full dataset of 16,000+ SNPs, I am having issues loading a genclone and probably have to switch to genlight objects.)

All the best and thank you for any input,
Jennifer
